facts.value: Sociological factors focus not on psychological attributes of learners but on their environment and position in society. They include socioeconomic status, ethnicity, cultural background, and gender.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Education in Educational Studies

facts.value: Socioeconomic status depends on income but includes other factors, such as financial security, social status, social class, and quality of life attributes.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Education in Educational Studies

facts.value: Low socioeconomic status affects educational success in various ways. It is linked to slower cognitive developments in language and memory and higher dropout rates. Poor families may not have enough money to meet basic nutritional needs of their children, lack means to invest in educational resources, and may be unable to afford tuition at prestigious schools.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Education in Educational Studies

facts.value: Students from an economically disadvantaged background may be forced to dropout from school to provide income to their families.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Education in Educational Studies

facts.value: Low socioeconomic status is linked to lower physical and mental health.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Education in Educational Studies

facts.value: Ethnic background is linked to cultural differences and language barriers, making it more difficult for students to adapt to the school environment and follow classes.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Education in Educational Studies

facts.value: Explicit and implicit biases and discrimination toward ethnic minorities may affect students' self-esteem and motivation as well as their access to educational opportunities.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Education in Educational Studies

facts.value: Historically, gender has been a central factor in education since the roles of men and women were defined differently in many societies.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Education in Educational Studies

facts.value: Education tended to strongly favor men, who were expected to provide for the family. Women were expected to manage the household and rear children, barring most educational opportunities available to them.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Education in Educational Studies

facts.value: Expectations associated with stereotypes can work both on an external level and an internal level, possibly leading to self-fulfilling prophecies.
